hints: Y and Z are isotopes of the same element.
Isotopes of one element have the same number of protons, and nuclear charge depends on proton number.
walkthrough: As isotopes of the same element, Y and Z have equal numbers of protons.
A nucleus's positive charge is determined by its number of protons.
Therefore, Y has the same charge as Z.

ai_rubric.observable: States that Y and Z have the same number of protons and therefore the same charge.

hints: An alpha particle contains two protons.
Compare the number of protons before and after alpha emission, then relate proton number to nuclear charge.
walkthrough: Alpha emission removes two protons from nucleus X to form nucleus Y.
Nucleus Y consequently has two fewer protons than X.
Its nuclear charge is therefore less than that of X.

ai_rubric.observable: States that Y has two fewer protons than X.
States that Y has less charge than X.

hints: The isolated parent nucleus X is initially stationary, so the total momentum before decay is zero.
After decay, the alpha particle and nucleus Y must have momenta that sum to zero.
walkthrough: Nucleus X is initially stationary, so the total momentum before decay is zero.
Momentum is conserved for the isolated decay, so the total momentum after decay must also be zero.
The emitted alpha particle has momentum, so nucleus Y must have equal and opposite momentum; Y cannot be stationary.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the total momentum before decay is zero because X is stationary.
Explains that Y must have momentum equal and opposite to the alpha particle, so Y cannot be stationary.
